title: Add a cross-process pane-split lock module
action: Create packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/herding/split_lock.rs: a cross-process advisory lock so concurrent `bee herding run` PROCESSES serialize their pane split. Each spawn is its own OS process, so an in-process Mutex cannot work; the lock must be a file. Model it on the store-lock already in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/hooks/prompt_context.rs - read `fn try_acquire` (create_new + AlreadyExists), `fn try_stale_takeover`, `fn is_pid_alive`/`fn pid_alive_os` (both the #[cfg(windows)] and #[cfg(unix)] arms), `fn random_token`, and `struct LockGuard` with its `fn release`. Do NOT refactor prompt_context.rs and do NOT make its private items public: write a self-contained module in herding/. Shape: lock file at <main_root>/.bee/locks/herding-pane-split.lock holding {pid, ts, token, job_id}; `pub(crate) fn acquire(main_root: &Path, job_id: &str, wait: Duration) -> Result<Option<SplitLock>, String>` that retries every 50ms until the wait budget is spent, returning Ok(None) on budget exhaustion (never an Err - the caller fails open) and Err only on a real filesystem failure; a stale holder is taken over when its recorded pid is dead, or when the lock file's mtime is older than a hard-stale ceiling (keep the two-tier rule prompt_context.rs uses: a soft window where a live pid still holds, a hard ceiling where it does not). `pub(crate) struct SplitLock` releases in `impl Drop`, and - like LockGuard::release - removes the file ONLY when the on-disk holder still carries this acquisition's own pid and token. Create the .bee/locks directory if absent. Add `mod split_lock;` to packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/herding.rs beside the existing `mod run;` line, keeping the file's existing doc-comment-per-mod style. Tests in the module's own #[cfg(test)] block, using a temp directory: (a) a second acquire while a live holder is held returns Ok(None) within the budget; (b) the lock is re-acquirable after the first guard drops; (c) a holder file naming a dead pid with an old mtime is taken over; (d) a real contention test - N threads each acquire, increment a shared counter, assert the counter was never observed concurrently, and release - proving mutual exclusion over the actual file.

truths: Two concurrent acquire calls against the same lock file never both hold it
